correctness.rationale: For every real strictly proper candidate, p_λ(z)=z^n−σ−λd(z) is monic. Bounding the product of its n roots at μ and L by ρ^n and using Lp_μ(0)−μp_L(0)=−σ(L−μ) gives ρ^n≥(L−μ)/(L+μ). The constant numerator −2σ/(L+μ) makes p_λ(z)=z^n−σ(1−2λ/(L+μ)), attaining that bound exactly at either endpoint, including the repeated zero-root case at the midpoint. The optimizer satisfies the same signed n-step recurrence as b_k. Its subtraction gives the stated linear error recurrence, so interleaved error subsequences have factor at most q=(L−μ)/(L+μ) per block, and a nonzero endpoint mode realizes it in the worst case. Line 44 incorrectly writes equality between the fixed-A spectral norm and the maximum over the whole allowable interval; only ≤ is true in general, as obtained from the maximum over spec(A). That local correction immediately proves the same bound and does not change the theorem. The argument is exact for either sign and does not require n≥4.
residual_risks: The rate is worst-case over the full curvature interval and does not assert equality for every fixed Hessian or every initialization. No rate claim for more general controllers or forcing is assessed.

equivalent_formulations.reasoning: Replace w by z^n in either filter. Its closed-loop polynomial is the linear polynomial w−σ(1−αλ) evaluated at z^n. Every root w produces nth roots z of modulus |w|^(1/n), with the zero case also immediate. The filter remains real and strictly proper and has no canceled model poles. This gives the same constant numerator and same worst-case factor for each sign, including even n. The alternative z→−z equivalence only applies to odd n and is not needed.
